title: Air India Says Airspace Curbs Are Worse Than Last Year as Gulf Closures Push Flights South
excerpt: Pakistan's closure was the first detour; restrictions over Saudi Arabia, Kuwait and the Iran conflict zone now add fuel, stopovers and surcharges on long-haul routes.
body:
• Air India says the impact of airspace closures is now worse than last year, as Gulf curbs add to the Pakistan closure on its Europe and North America routes, PTI reported.
  • Flights are being pushed further south, raising fuel burn; some services need a stopover, adding landing charges on top.
  • The airline could not quantify the financial impact, a senior official said on October 12.
  • For new bookings from October 9, Air India's fuel surcharge is $215 one-way to North America, $135 to Europe and the UK, and $55 to West Asia — check the surcharge line before paying.

Air India is facing a bigger hit from airspace closures than it did last year, a senior airline official said on Monday, as restrictions linked to the Middle East conflict layer on top of the Pakistan airspace closure that has shaped its long-haul network since early last year. The official described a "big impact" that is hard to quantify, in remarks reported by PTI via the Nagaland Post.

"The more airspaces are closed, the more southwards flights have to go — the more the fuel bill."

— Senior Air India official, via PTI

Two closures, one long way round

The Tata Group airline has flown longer routes to Europe and North America since Pakistan closed its airspace to Indian carriers early last year. Now, the official said, the Iran conflict has added restrictions in Gulf countries including Saudi Arabia and Kuwait. Each closed corridor pushes flights further south, which means more flying hours and more fuel burned on every departure. On some flights the extra distance forces a stopover, which adds landing charges and crew costs to the fuel bill.

What passengers are already paying

Part of the cost is already visible in ticket prices. Air India and Air India Express raised fuel surcharges on new bookings from October 9, citing aviation turbine fuel prices and operating costs. The one-way international surcharges are $215 for North America, $210 for Australia, $135 for Europe including the UK and $55 for West Asia and the Middle East, according to Travel World Online's summary of the revised charges. Domestic surcharges run from Rs 400 to Rs 1,200 by distance. The airlines said the charges will be reviewed as fuel prices and market conditions change.

For diaspora travellers

For the India–North America and India–Europe routes the diaspora uses most, the practical effects are three: longer scheduled flight times on westbound services, occasional technical stops that do not appear in older timetables, and the new surcharge line in the fare break-up. If you are booking Diwali or December travel, compare total fares rather than base fares — the surcharge differences between carriers that have revised charges and those that have not can be the margin. Travellers with tight onward connections should also allow extra buffer while routings remain fluid, a point our coverage of Saudi flight cancellations through October 17 sets out in detail.

What to watch

The official gave no figure for the financial damage, and none was available in the reporting. The variables are external: any reopening of Gulf corridors shortens routes immediately, while a further spread of closures pushes flights still further south. Until then, Air India's long-haul economics — and its passengers' journey times — are set by other countries' skies.
